problem: Panoramic VLN models perform strongly but need panoramic cameras that many robots lack, while existing monocular VLN models are too weak for practical use, leaving a sim-to-real gap for monocular robots.
motivation: Monocular robots have a limited field of view and cannot directly run high-performing panoramic models. Giving them panoramic-like perception would let them reuse those models without new hardware.
key_idea: Equip a monocular robot with panoramic perception by fusing multi-view images into navigable maps to predict waypoints, then synthesizing new-view representations at those waypoints with a dynamic ray sampling NeRF, so that panoramic VLN models can be transferred to the monocular setting.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that widening the effective field of view through multi-view fusion and NeRF view synthesis, rather than redesigning the navigation policy, is what closes the monocular-panoramic gap.
method: Multi-view image input: uses several monocular views to expand the limited field of view of a monocular robot.
Multi-map adaptive fusion module: fuses multiple navigable maps and updates them to predict agent-centered navigable waypoints.
Dynamic ray sampling NeRF: generates new-view representations at the predicted waypoints, giving panoramic-like features.
Transfer of panoramic models: the resulting representations feed a high-performance panoramic VLN model, so it runs on monocular systems.

setting.backbone: not specified in the abstract (a panoramic VLN model transferred to monocular input, with a NeRF-based view generator)

results: The abstract states that the method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art monocular VLN methods on R2R-CE. No numbers are given.
